issues: Both quotes and both evidence strings re-checked: FOUND. Title, Date of Publication (19 November 2021), DOI 10.1109/IEEESTD.2021.9618905 and kind match. IEEE SA records Board Approval 2021-09-23 and Published 2021-11-19 (--check FOUND). Listed on the GET series page.

The note's claim that the employee appears 'as a "data subject" who needs to understand how their data is handled, not as a party who acts' is contradicted by the rest of the purpose, which Xplore cuts off ('...the means used to protect the data s...'). A reseller copy of IEEE's text (en-standard.eu, --check FOUND) continues: 'Each issue is addressed in terms of the means used to protect the data subject's personal data and the data subject's options if the personal data is compromised. Inspired by the European Union (EU) General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) legislation, the standard is designed so that workers ... will have control and influence over the personal information that directly represents a core asset of their identity and lives'. The stated design aim gives workers options, control and influence. The note is rewritten.

The summary is one-sided and slightly misattributes. It lists only the employer's data uses ('help employers access, collect, store, use, share and destroy employee data'). It leaves out the transparency aim in the title and purpose, and the stated aim of worker control. It also runs the 'metrics and conformance criteria' into 'to help employers access...', although the abstract ties them to 'these types of uses from trusted global partners and how third parties and employers can meet them'. The summary is rewritten from the abstract and the full purpose.
addressedTo 'organisation' stands: the abstract addresses employers and the purpose 'organizations'. personalData 'central' stands, and the full purpose strengthens it.

fieldFixes.summary: Describes methodologies, with metrics and conformance criteria, for how employers access, collect, store, use, share and destroy employee data, in processes that can be explained to the employee as data subject; its stated purpose, inspired by the GDPR, is that workers have control and influence over their personal information.
fieldFixes.note: The employer runs the governance: the abstract addresses employers, and the purpose addresses 'organizations'. The employee is the data subject. On Xplore the purpose is cut off ('...'). Its remainder, read in a reseller copy of IEEE's text (en-standard.eu), says each issue is addressed in terms of 'the data subject's options if the personal data is compromised'. It adds that, inspired by the GDPR, the standard 'is designed so that workers ... will have control and influence over the personal information' about them. So the worker is given options and influence within governance the employer runs. What those options are, and whether workers have any part in setting the terms, would need the full PDF, which was not read. Certification processes, success criteria and execution procedures are stated to be out of scope.
